Subject: Subprocessor info and audit rights request

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week — FinServe is moving fast and legal asked me to gather a few privacy artifacts before we progress to procurement. Can Redwood provide the following by end of next week?

- Current subprocessor inventory with subprocessors' purpose and countries
- DPA (latest) and any redline-friendly format (DocuSign link is fine)
- Confirmation of audit/access rights under Art.28 (remote evidence preferred)
- A sample Art.30 processing record export or template we can include with our DPIA

If there's a standard schedule for a remote evidence review (SOC2 + logs + processing map), please propose dates. We will also need the procurement contact to confirm timelines.

Appreciate it — Oliver

Hi Oliver — thanks, we can support this. At a high level:

- Attached are the current DPA (Redwood-DPA-v3.pdf) and our published subprocessor list (subprocessor-list-202602.pdf).
- We support auditor access; typical flow is remote evidence first (logs, configs, redacted dataflow), with an on-site option in constrained cases.
- We'll include an export of our Art.30 processing records (redacted) and a technical processing map.

Action items I propose:
1) Marissa (legal) will send the DPA redline workflow and DocuSign link.
2) Karthik (privacy/infra) will prepare the Art.30 export + processing map and propose 2x remote evidence windows next week.
3) I'll coordinate with Procurement on timeline and any PO/contract items.

Can you confirm whether FinServe needs the full SOC2 report or a SOC2 + ISO summary? Also flag any special data residency controls (e.g., no transfers outside UK/EU) so we can surface any limitations.

Thanks,
Evelyn

Oliver — looping in legal.

Per Evelyn's note, we can share the DPA via DocuSign for redlines. A couple of quick points to set expectations:

- Our standard DPA includes an Article 28 subprocessor clause and audit provisions that allow remote evidence review. On-site audits are considered case-by-case and typically require an NDA + scheduling window.
- We cannot provide access to raw production data; evidence is redacted or scoped to logs/configs, and we provide sampling where needed.
- For Art.30, we will share a redacted export suitable for your DPIA; operational records (detailed configs) will be provided in a remote evidence packet.

I'll send the DocuSign link and our review timeline (48-72 business hours for initial redline review). If FinServe's legal wants specific contract language changes, please have them mark the DocuSign review or send formal redlines to this thread.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa / Evelyn — that sounds good. A few clarifications from our side:

- FinServe prefers remote evidence first. For SOC2 we need the full report and bridge letters where available; ISO summary is nice-to-have but not sufficient alone.
- For Art.28 audit rights, the DPO specifically wants confirmation that Redwood's subprocessors sign equivalent data protection obligations and that FinServe can request auditor access limited to customer-scoped data and configs.
- The DPIA team would like a simple CSV export for the Art.30 fields (processing activity, categories, legal basis, transfers) that we can import into our DPIA tool.

Can you confirm the earliest remote evidence window (90-120 min) you can offer next week? Procurement will need a target date for the contract flow as well.

Oliver

Summary of what we can provide in a remote evidence session (90–120 minutes):

- System architecture diagram, dataflow map, and list of active subprocessors (we already provided the list)

Notes on limitations: on-site access requires an executed DPA + scheduler and a minimum 30-day lead time. We do not allow extraction of raw production datasets; any sample data is synthetic or redacted.

- Tue 17 Feb 2026, 09:00–11:00 CET
